title: Motives of corporate location choice (chapter)
outlet: The Hungarian Labour Market 2004 (Fazekas, Koltay, Cseres-Gergely eds.)
summary_en: Where do firms locate, and why? Békés contributes a chapter on corporate location choice to the 2004 Hungarian Labour Market Yearbook (Munkaerőpiaci Tükör). Drawing on firm-level data and the international location-choice literature, the chapter reviews the determinants of where Hungarian firms set up — proximity to suppliers and customers, labour-cost differentials, infrastructure, and agglomeration economies — and discusses the implications for regional labour-market disparities in Hungary.
policy_relevance: Background reference for Hungarian regional and labour-market policy (NGM, HIPA, Belügyminisztérium county-level economic-development arm): the chapter frames why some Hungarian regions (Northern Transdanubia, Budapest) attract firm activity while others (Eastern Hungary) lag. Foundational input for HIPA's location-promotion strategy and for active labour-market programmes calibrated to lagging counties.
